mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate) of the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan Region is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Use notarization by a Taiwan notary followed by cross-strait verification through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); this is the functional equivalent of consular legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions. Never add a Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Paid-in Capital, No Dissolution Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certificate in Taiwan, then verify through SEF/ARATS (cross-strait consular legalization substitute). Do not use Hague Apostille because Taiwan Region is not an Apostille Convention party.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE legal representative and bank signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the board resolution/PoA before a Taiwan notary, then verify through SEF/ARATS. This path is the parallel alternative to Hague Apostille for non-member states; do not chain an Apostille after consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (notarized copy) of the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize a full copy in Taiwan, then verify via SEF/ARATS. No Hague Apostille applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Taiwan funding bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter must be current within 90 days; the bank's signature is notarized in Taiwan and then verified via SEF/ARATS. Apostille is not applicable to Taiwan-issued documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Ownership Structure Chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the UBO declaration in Taiwan and verify via SEF/ARATS. The declaration must identify all individuals exercising 25% or more control. No Hague Apostille is to be attached.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners holding 25% or more must be screened in real time against OFAC SDN/SSI lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated sanctions list, PRC Ministry of Public Security anti-money laundering watchlists, SAMR/PBOC beneficial-owner disqualification lists, and Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission sanctions lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for political exposed persons (PEPs), including senior mainland officials, Taiwan legislative/executive personnel, SOE executives, and their family members. Screening must cover aliases, previous names, passport numbers, residential addresses, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth; false declarations trigger criminal AML liability and denial of registration. Ongoing monitoring is required for the life of the WFOE.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (R.O.C.), administered through the regional National Taxation Bureaus; the online electronic filing and information services are provided through the MOF Tax e-Filing Portal and the Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity forming a WFOE Ltd in Taiwan, first obtain investment approval from the Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission and complete MOEA company registration. After incorporation, file Business Tax Registration with the local National Taxation Bureau, submitting the articles of incorporation, foreign investor certificate, board resolution appointing a local statutory representative, address proof or lease for the business premises, bank account information, and foreign investor remittance certificate. The Taxation Bureau then issues the eight-digit Unified Number, which is the national Taxpayer Identification Number, together with a Business Tax Registration Certificate. Where the foreign non-resident entity has no fixed place of business or agent in Taiwan and supplies only cross-border electronic services, the MOF Taxation Administration registers the foreign entity in the simplified non-resident electronic-services taxpayer system and issues a withholding payment account or Unified Number for reverse-charge compliance. The WFOE must notify the Taxation Bureau of any registration amendments, address changes, or representative changes within 15 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election purposes. A qualifying enterprise may elect the special small-business Business Tax regime at 1% if average monthly taxable sales remain below NT$200,000, but that regime is not available to a WFOE exporting zero-rated goods; the standard VAT invoice-and-input-credit regime is mandatory for exporters.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax under the Business Tax Act (Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$200,000 average monthly taxable sales is the threshold above which standard Value-Added Business Tax registration and Uniform Invoice issuance are mandatory; below this threshold a small-business special tax status at 1% may apply. There is no blanket exemption from registration for any person carrying on a business selling goods or services in Taiwan.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Standard VAT-registered businesses must issue Uniform Invoices. The MOF Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform receives e-invoice data through the Electronic Invoice Turnkey service and machine-readable API transmission. E-invoices carry an electronic encryption token and invoice QR anti-tampering mechanism. B2C e-invoices from designated electronic-commerce and internet businesses must be uploaded to the national platform within the statutory period, generally within 48 hours of issuance, while B2B invoices must be transmitted within the applicable filing window. Taiwan does not use real-time fiscal stamping equipment; anti-fraud control is achieved through central platform receipt, cryptographic integrity, QR verification, and periodic Business Tax filing reconciliation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, goods actually exported from Taiwan after Customs clearance, goods supplied outside Taiwan, and services used entirely outside Taiwan and paid in foreign currency qualify for the 0% Business Tax rate. A WFOE may claim export zero-rating only if the goods physically leave Taiwan, the Taiwan Customs export declaration is in the WFOE name, title and risk pass to the overseas buyer, and the sale proceeds are received in foreign currency. Offshore digital services can qualify where the place of supply is outside Taiwan and the recipient is a foreign territory; services consumed in Taiwan remain taxable at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Bill of Export) with the Taiwan Customs serial number
Signed commercial invoice and packing list
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing the WFOE as shipper and the overseas buyer as consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Taiwan authorized-bank Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate evidencing repatriation of export proceeds in foreign currency
Original sales contract or purchase order showing the export terms, foreign buyer, and destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, if the customs export proof or foreign exchange repatriation evidence is missing, incomplete, or false, the zero-rating is reversed, the 5% Business Tax is reassessed, and interest runs from the original tax filing due date. Under the Business Tax Act and the Tax Collection Act, the taxpayer may face a penalty of up to five times the short-paid tax. Deliberate falsification of an export declaration or inward remittance certificate constitutes tax evasion and may trigger criminal liability, asset preservation measures, and suspension or revocation of business tax registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China. Although the parent shareholder sits in Taiwan, the WFOE is an onshore PRC entity and is therefore governed by PRC foreign exchange regulations, not Taiwan's central bank rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with a central parity fixing and a daily trading band against the USD. Current account items, such as export proceeds, service fees, wages and lawfully distributed dividends, are effectively convertible through authorized banks under an authenticity and rational-necessity review. Capital account items are not freely convertible. Inbound foreign direct investment must be registered with SAFE through a domestic designated bank, after which the WFOE may open a capital account facility and convert paid-in equity into RMB only under bank supervision. Outbound capital movements, including shareholder loan repayments, equity disposal proceeds, and liquidation distributions, require separate SAFE approvals or deregistration procedures. Profit remittance to the Taiwanese shareholder is achievable only after the WFOE completes its statutory audit, files corporate income tax returns, resolves retained earnings via shareholder resolution, and settles any dividend withholding tax. The remitting bank will require the audit report, tax payment vouchers, board/shareholder resolution, and a valid foreign exchange payment declaration. The RMB is not freely convertible outside the onshore clearing system, although cross-border RMB settlement is permitted for bona fide trade and FDI structures where the Taiwanese counterparty agrees to RMB.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China abolished mandatory export proceeds surrender and there is no minimum conversion ratio. The WFOE may retain 100% of its export foreign currency receipts in an approved foreign currency settlement account, or it may convert them into RMB at the onshore market rate. If receipts are brought onshore or retained without an offshore-holding approval, the full amount must be declared under the trade current account and matched against customs declarations. The banking system performs the SAFE trade payment and collection declaration, normally on the day of receipt, with correction and verification obligation completed no later than five business days after settlement. No statutory forced conversion timeline applies. Delinquent declaration can result in the suspension of trade payment functions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability and legally barred for onshore WFOE clearing. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not licensed by the PBOC to open CNY-denominated accounts, hold deposits for a PRC entity, execute SAFE trade/financial declarations, or settle capital account flows. They cannot participate in CNAPS, CIPS, or the onshore interbank FX market. The WFOE may use such EMIs only as informal information dashboards or for expenses outside China, but all statutory liquidity clearing, FX conversion, and AML-controllable payments must route through a licensed domestic Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical in-branch interview. The WFOE legal representative must appear personally before the branch compliance officer for a face-to-face KYC interview and sign account opening documents under the company seal. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted under the PBOC basic deposit account rules. A notarized power of attorney can authorize a second signer to handle administrative filings only after the legal representative's identity has been verified in person. Some pilot branches permit supplementary video verification, but the in-person interview is not waived for an onshore WFOE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity around the Taiwanese parent holding structure and inability to identify the ultimate natural person owners, triggering enhanced due diligence for the WFOE as a foreign-invested entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation, current memorandum and articles of association, full shareholder register, board resolution approving the China investment, passport copies of all natural person UBOs and directors, six-month source-of-funds bank statements, audited financial statements of the Taiwanese parent, tax residency certificates, and a complete corporate structure diagram showing each intermediate company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared plush toy OEM business and high-volume low-value invoicing, or invoice prices that deviate materially from arms-length fair market value, suggesting trade-based money laundering or transfer mispricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full order lifecycle file: executed OEM/ODM manufacturing agreements, purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists, customs export declarations with electronic port data, bills of lading or airway bills, container counts, inspection certifications, third-party quality reports, independent benchmark pricing for comparable stuffed plush toys, and transfer pricing documentation aligned with PRC tax rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Plush mascots bearing cartoon characters, sports marks, or entertainment IP where authorized production cannot be evidenced, creating counterfeit goods exposure and reputational/sanctions risk in trade finance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized IP licensing agreements from the trademark/copyright owners, royalty schedules, distribution authorizations, trademark and copyright registration certificates, product prototype images, customs commodity classification codes, and where applicable, export control or sanctions clearance letters confirming no restricted or prohibited party involvement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concern that inbound FDI equity capital may be recycled to the Taiwan parent, misused for unauthorized domestic investment, or converted to RMB outside SAFE-approved capital account purpose, violating PRC foreign exchange rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration confirmation issued through the receiving bank, inward remittance receipt with the correct SAFE capital account purpose code, board-approved capital utilization plan, capital account ledger, monthly accounting records, Chinese CPA audited capital verification report, valid tax e-filing certificates, and a signed undertaking committing all funds to working capital, fixed asset purchases, and bona fide WFOE operating expenses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before remittance, the Taiwanese shareholder must complete any applicable Taiwan Investment Commission authorization for mainland investment. The WFOE then completes FDI foreign exchange registration with SAFE through the nominated domestic bank and opens a capital account facility. The Taiwan parent must instruct a SWIFT MT103 wire to the WFOE capital account using the bank-declared SAFE foreign exchange purpose code for direct investment equity contribution, with the remitter name and beneficiary account precisely matching the FDI registration. The receiving bank verifies the SWIFT header, source jurisdiction, transaction purpose code, and registration reference. After credit and bank-level capital verification, an onshore certified public accountant issues the capital verification report confirming paid-in capital. Any RMB conversion from the capital account requires a separate bank-supervised settlement instruction evidencing the lawful capital usage purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to Taiwanese suppliers and third-party component vendors must be processed through the current account trade settlement rail. For open account arrangements, the WFOE instructs its domestic bank to send a SWIFT MT103 remittance carrying the applicable SAFE trade payment purpose code, supported by the sales contract, commercial invoice, packing list, customs declaration, and logistics documentation. For larger procurement or where the supplier requires bank assurance, the WFOE may open an irrevocable commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700; documentary collections with documents against payment or documents against acceptance are also permissible for established counterparties. All outbound disbursements must reconcile with the customs database and tax filing status. For cross-border RMB settlements to Taiwan, the payment can clear through CNAPS and CIPS, with the Taiwan beneficiary receiving RMB through an authorized RMB clearing bank. US dollar and other foreign currency settlements clear through SWIFT, correspondent banking, and CHIPS/Fedwire networks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts for genuine trade and approved capital-account exposures, executed through a bank with interbank FX market membership

Onshore foreign exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps for balance-sheet hedging of approved foreign-currency debt or FDI-related financial exposures, limited to the notional and maturity of the underlying exposure
Plain-vanilla European-style CNY/USD options purchased from authorized banks on a real-demand basis for hedging, not for speculative open positions

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted onshore for a PRC WFOE because the RMB delivery obligation must be settled onshore; offshore NDFs also cannot be used to hedge the WFOE's onshore trade or capital flows under PRC foreign exchange law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Information Declaration under Article 22-1 of the Taiwan Company Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (electronic filing gateway)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 1 to March 31 annually, reporting company data as of December 31 of the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing: administrative fine of NTD 50,000 to NTD 500,000 (approx. USD 1,700 to 8,300) per instance; order to rectify within a deadline; subsequent failure to rectify may result in increased fines up to NTD 2,000,000 (approx. USD 33,300); persistent violation may lead to registration restrictions or a court-ordered compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return including Undistributed Surplus Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (regional office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 to May 31 each year for a calendar-year fiscal year end (December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 1% for every 2 days overdue, capped at 15% of the assessed tax, plus statutory interest; additional penalty of NTD 1,500 to NTD 45,000 for late filing when no tax is due; under-reporting penalty of up to 200% of the understated tax; enforcement including garnishment of bank accounts and seizure of assets for non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members (AGM) with approval of financial statements and surplus distribution/appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; minutes and supporting records retained at the company's registered office for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., no later than June 30 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors are subject to a fine of NTD 10,000 to NTD 50,000 (approx. USD 330 to 1,650) for failure to convene within the statutory period; shareholders may petition the court to order a shareholder meeting, with the company bearing the associated costs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit by a licensed CPA is legally mandatory when the company's paid-in capital exceeds NTD 50 million (approx. USD 1.6 million), or when the company's annual net revenue exceeds NTD 100 million (approx. USD 3.3 million), or when total assets exceed NTD 300 million (approx. USD 10 million). The competent authority may also designate any company for audit if required by law or for public interest. For the referenced WFOE (assumed paid-in capital below NTD 50 million, non-regulated, low-risk), no compulsory audit is triggered unless one of these quantitative thresholds is exceeded.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan IFRS (for public companies) or the Enterprise Accounting Standard (Taiwan GAAP based on IFRS for SMEs) for non-public limited companies; full IFRS is also permissible on a voluntary basis. Financial statements must be prepared in New Taiwan Dollars on an accrual basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Pursuant to Article 22-1 of the Taiwan Company Act, the company must annually confirm (during the fixed March 1-31 declaration window) the full list of directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of the paid-in capital. This declaration serves as the definitive UBO annual confirmation and must be updated in the system within 15 days of any change in ownership or management, with the next annual declaration reflecting the updated data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 2,500 per annum for a registered office/agent in Taiwan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 8,000 per annum for a statutory audit by a CPA in Taiwan (if the capital/revenue threshold is triggered; otherwise voluntary audit fees may be lower)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general zero-rate tax holiday. Applicable incentives include the 15% preferential rate for High and New Technology Enterprises, the reduced effective 5% rate for Small and Low-Profit Enterprises (annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, as extended to 2027), and a 100% additional deduction for qualified R&D expenses.
